message.reasoning:
I'm working through recreating the layout of this old 1900 Brazilian newspaper page, starting with the header details and transcribing the three-column body text about official government correspondence.

Continuing through more payment authorizations to the Repartição de Aguas e Exgottos for various suppliers of materials and articles in February, including Espindola Siqueira, Hildebrand, Bastiano Buona Vita, Eduardo Kneesse, and Kisgen & Schiefferdecker.

Continuing through the list of payments, I'm noting more entries for supplies to the same office, gas service for the Water and Sewage Department, materials furnished, and forage payments to various suppliers throughout February.

Then there's a credit of 3:311$200 to the amanuensis João Alfredo Baptista Borba covering February expenses for engineer per diems and transport, with him returning a small balance to the treasury, followed by an advance of 680$750 to engineer Victor Andrigo for roof repairs at the Hospicio de Alienados.

Permission is granted to engineer Antonio By to deposit 300$000 as guarantee for his proposal to build a jail in S. Bento do Sapucahy, the Geographic and Geological Commission is authorized to spend 3:200$000 on eight animals for field crews, and the contract with Francisco José do Prado for ferry service on the Parahyba river is approved.

The bills from Erico Milla & Comp. are returned to the Water and Sewage Department for correction. Today, March 31, 1900, the proposals for building the S. Bento do Sapucahy jail were opened, submitted by Antonio By, Nicola Grigola, Santiago Stornini, José Mollica, and Santo Bertollazzi, and referred to the board for further decision. A request from the City of Santos Improvements Company, Limited is also noted.

The company's petition seeks reconsideration of the February 22nd order, presenting a bill of 7:500$000 for water supplied for fire extinguishing and street irrigation in Santos during October, November, and December of 1899—the earlier order is maintained and payment is requisitioned. Now I'm moving into the Justice section's daily business for March 31, 1900, starting with the first sub-directorate's first section, which is transmitting a matter to the Minister of Justice and Interior Affairs.

This includes forwarding a rogatory letter from a judge in Santa Cruz do Rio Pardo to authorities in Melgaço, Portugal, regarding the citation of an heir in an estate inventory case, plus a communication to the Interior Secretary about an inquiry from a justice of the peace in Caçapava concerning upcoming electoral registration, and a related notice sent to the police chief.

I'm noting a report that a citizen, Adolpho Schumann, is illegally practicing pharmacy in Jacarehy after acquiring a pharmacy from another licensed pharmacist, with instructions to proceed against him under the penal code. There's also a dispatched notice from a judge in Piedade forwarding a copy of an edict opening a competition for notary and land registry official positions.

I'm also seeing requests for information from judges in Mogy-mirim, Itatiba, and Botucatú regarding pardon petitions filed by sentenced individuals—Heitor des Retours, Paulo Luiz, and another still being noted—each accompanied by the respective judge's opinion.

I'm noting he requests a copy of his case file to support a clemency petition. I'm also seeing the case forwarded to the president of the Tribunal de Justiça requesting information on Antonio Augusto Alves's clemency petition, related to his sentence from the Bebedouro jury.

Now I'm building an HTML table with three columns and bordered cells to organize the remaining transmittals: the appointment title for Bananal's public prosecutor Alvaro Augusto de Carvalho Aranha as curador geral of orphans, and a similar title for Xiririca's public prosecutor.
